title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives election for North Carolina's 12th Congressional District
description: The 2026 election for North Carolina's 12th Congressional District pits incumbent Democrat Alma Adams against Republican challenger Jack Codiga. The district, which covers most of Charlotte and surrounding areas in Mecklenburg County, was redrawn under new maps passed by the Republican-led legislature in October 2025. Adams has held the seat since winning a special election in 2014 and is seeking her seventh full term, while Codiga is a first-time candidate and financial professional making his electoral debut. Cook Political Report rates the district as Solidly Democratic, reflecting its strong Democratic lean, though the newly drawn boundaries could shift the political dynamics.
polling_note: No general election polls were found for this race as of the research date. Cook Political Report rates the district as 'Solidly Democratic,' indicating the race is not considered competitive at this stage.

candidates.name: Alma Adams
candidates.summary: Alma Adams is the incumbent U.S. Representative for North Carolina's 12th Congressional District, first elected in a November 2014 special election. A former art professor and college administrator at Bennett College, she served in the North Carolina House of Representatives for over 20 years before going to Congress. Adams is a member of the House Agriculture Committee and the House Education and Workforce Committee, and has focused on historically Black colleges and universities, voting rights, and economic equity during her tenure.

candidates.name: Jack Codiga
candidates.summary: Jack Codiga is a Republican candidate running for U.S. House in North Carolina's 12th Congressional District. He is a financial professional working in real estate capital markets at Medalist Capital in Charlotte, with prior experience at Bridge Bank. Codiga won the Republican primary on March 3, 2026, defeating challenger Addul Ali, and is making his first run for elected office on a platform focused on economic freedom, lower cost of living, and limited government.

forecast.rationale: No general-election polling exists, which inherently limits certainty. However, the available contextual indicators are overwhelming: Alma Adams is a longtime incumbent seeking her seventh full term with a strong incumbency track record; Cook Political Report rates NC-12 as 'Solidly Democratic'; the Republican challenger Jack Codiga is a first-time candidate with no prior electoral experience; and the district (covering most of Charlotte/Mecklenburg County) has a heavily Democratic partisan lean, even after the 2025 redistricting by the Republican-led legislature. While sparse polling and redistricting introduce some uncertainty, the combination of incumbency, partisanship, and rating firmly supports a safe Democratic outcome.
